summary: At an average annual temperature of 38°F and a night low of 28°F, Mammoth Lakes is one of the coldest incorporated places in California — a town where winter isn't a season but a defining fact of life, with snow measured in feet per storm along the eastern Sierra Nevada at roughly 7,900 feet of elevation. The economy orbits around Mammoth Mountain ski area and the outdoor recreation it feeds: lodging, food service, retail, and resort operations form the employment backbone, which means most jobs are tied to the same industry and switching employers without leaving town is genuinely constrained. A median home price of $657,000 against a median household income of $87,121 yields a price-to-income ratio above 7.5, steep by any standard — and much of the housing stock doubles as vacation rental inventory, compressing what's available for year-round occupancy. The town itself is compact at roughly 7,100 residents spread across 25 square miles, with trail access to the Inyo National Forest essentially from the edges of town and 9.3 hours of daily sunshine cutting through thin, dry mountain air. The food and retail scene reflects a resort economy: restaurants and coffee shops cluster along Main Street (Highway 203), but grocery and everyday shopping options are limited for a place this isolated — the nearest full-service city, Bishop, sits about 40 miles south. Mammoth Lakes is less a traditional town than a small, beautiful settlement whose economy, housing market, and daily rhythms are all downstream of the mountain that gives it its name.
